root_idea.summary: The root centers on inclination or deviation, extending from bodily crookedness to turning away from error toward upright religious commitment.
root_idea.development: The physical sense of bending or inward deviation develops metaphorically into moral and religious orientation: the ḥanīf turns from falsehood toward the straight and true way.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is a distinct lexical item with singular حَنِيف and plural حُنَفَاء; the singular is the appropriate public citation form.

senses.definition: Inclining away from error or falsehood toward uprightness and the true way.
senses.usage_conditions: A religious-moral description, often used adverbially or adjectivally for a person’s orientation toward the upright way; the plural is حُنَفَاء.

senses.definition: A committed adherent of Abraham’s monotheistic way; a Muslim devoted to the worship of the one God.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic contexts associated with Abraham, Islam, and rejection of idolatry; the expression identifies religious allegiance rather than bodily form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline or turn toward something, or to decline or turn away from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general physical or directional verb; the complement may be introduced with إِلَى or عَنْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have the bodily distortion called حَنَف, especially a crooked or inwardly turned leg or foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a physical condition rather than moral or religious uprightness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a person, leg, or foot أَحْنَف, causing or giving it the characteristic crookedness of حَنَف.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use applied to a person or to a leg or foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To follow the ḥanīf way or the Abrahamic law; also to become circumcised, turn away from idolatry, devote oneself to God, or apply oneself to religious exercises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A religious or ritual reflexive construction with several closely related classical applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A natural or acquired crookedness or wryness, especially an inward inversion or turning of the leg, foot, or great toe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe walking on the outer side of the foot or an inward inclination of its front.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A right state, condition, or tendency, understood as an inclination away from error toward what is right.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative and interpretive extension of the physical notion of inclination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person belonging to the school or tenets associated with Abū Ḥanīfah; Hanafi.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later juridical or sectarian affiliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person of the religion of Abraham.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah designation distinct from the Quranic headword حَنِيف.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel with a tap or a tap-equipped fountain used for ablution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-classical usage associated with ablution practices.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A type of sword associated with al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained as relating to the person who first ordered such swords to be made; variant forms are reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an older Arab convention, a person who had performed the pilgrimage or undergone circumcision and was thereby associated with Abraham’s religion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pre-Islamic or early conventional designation, not a restriction on the Quranic religious sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who devotes himself to religious exercises or worship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical devotional application of the adjective or noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Recent grounds of honor or prestige, belonging to the Islamic period rather than to ancient times.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression applied to حَسَب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate classical lexical use reported without a stated construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker of sandals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate occupational use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: According to some authorities, an inclination toward a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This explanation is explicitly disputed by another authority and should be treated as a reported, non-dominant interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The law or religious way of Abraham, identified with the religion of Islam.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in the expression مِلَّةٌ حَنِيفِيَّةٌ; this is the derived-nominal name of the religious way, distinct from the Quranic adjective حَنِيف.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the bodily distortion called حَنَف, especially a leg or foot that is crooked or whose great toe turns toward the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually applied to a person, with related feminine usage for a leg or foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A curved staff or stick, a bow, or a razor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These object names are explained by the curved shape associated with the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chameleon, a tortoise, a certain marine fish, or a certain tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A group of established naming applications reported separately from the bodily adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A changeable female slave, alternately lazy and brisk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Marked as a tropical usage in the lexical evidence.

cautions: The Quranic form is morphologically tagged as a noun in QAC but functions lexically as an adjective or substantive noun; its Quranic plural is حُنَفَاء.
The physical crookedness sense and the religious uprightness sense are historically related but are kept distinct in the public senses and classical coverage.
